title: Enhancing credit risk scorecards with transactional-based behavioural features
abstract: arXiv:2610.13199v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Background: Credit risk modelling is fundamental in financial institutions, typically using credit history, repayment behaviour, income, and outstanding debt to estimate a borrower's probability of default. Although transactional data are sometimes incorporated through aggregated measures such as recency, frequency, and monetary indicators, behavioural information embedded in raw transaction narratives remains largely unexplored due to its unstructured nature. This limits opportunities to extract richer behavioural insights.   Aim: This research investigates payment narratives from transactional data as an alternative data source for credit risk modelling.   Setting: The study uses transactional data from a large South African financial institution focused on small and medium enterprises. translated_title: 利用基于交易的行为特征增强信用风险评分卡
translated_abstract: 背景：信用风险建模是金融机构的基础工作，通常使用信用历史、还款行为、收入和未偿债务来估计借款人的违约概率。尽管交易数据有时会通过近期性、频率和金额等聚合指标被纳入模型，但嵌入在原始交易描述中的行为信息由于其非结构化的性质，在很大程度上仍未被开发利用。这限制了提取更丰富行为洞察的机会。研究目标：本研究探索将交易数据中的支付描述作为信用风险建模的替代数据源。研究背景：该研究使用了一家专注于中小型企业的南非大型金融机构的交易数据。研究方法：采用自然语言处理和正则表达式等技术，将非结构化的交易描述转换为有意义的……（原文摘要在此处截断）
tldr: 本研究利用自然语言处理和正则表达式技术，将非结构化的交易支付描述转化为行为特征，作为替代数据源来增强南非中小型企业信用风险评分卡的预测能力。
en_tdlr: This study leverages NLP and regular expression techniques to transform unstructured transaction payment narratives into behavioural features as an alternative data source for enhancing credit risk scorecards for SMEs at a large South African financial institution.
